description: We are a team of passionate full-stack and software developers united by our curiosity for space, technology, and innovation. With skills across web development, programming, data, and problem-solving, we combine our strengths to turn challenging ideas into practical solutions. We’re here to learn, build, experiment, and create something meaningful for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. 🚀
summary:
AstroKids Academy – Artemis-30: Moon Base Commander is an interactive, browser-based 3D space simulation for children aged 8–12. Young explorers discover space, interact with scientific environments, and manage a lunar outpost during a 30-day mission.

With an immersive, playful 3D aesthetic, the simulation blends space exploration, resource management, and interactive storytelling. As Moon Base Commander, players manage essential systems—Power, Oxygen, Food, and Crew Health—while facing environmental challenges and unexpected events.

The project makes complex aerospace concepts accessible to younger audiences by transforming passive reading into interactive decisions with visible consequences. Players must balance limited resources, prioritize critical systems, and adapt strategies to keep their lunar crew safe.

A key feature is integrating real scientific data through NASA's open resources. NASA's DONKI API provides space weather data, including solar flares and geomagnetic storms, translating these into mission alerts and educational challenges to show how real phenomena affect astronauts. Additional references from NASA's OSDR, RadLab, and the Canadian Space Agency support explanations of radiation exposure, biological research, and space food production.

By combining real scientific data, 3D exploration, and strategic gameplay, AstroKids Academy transforms space education into an engaging experience that fosters curiosity, critical thinking, and scientific awareness.
details:
Artemis-30: Moon Base Commander is an interactive educational simulation in which players become responsible for operating a lunar outpost over 30 in-game days. The experience combines a 3D space environment with mission-based gameplay, resource management, scientific challenges, and real-world space data.

Mission Cycle (Per In-Game Day / Sol):

  1. The Daily Log & Mission Briefing: Players receive a narrative captain's log introducing the day's objectives, environmental conditions, and potential mission challenges. Space weather information can be retrieved from NASA's DONKI API to provide real scientific context for the mission.
  2. Space Weather Monitoring: The system processes available space weather events, such as Coronal Mass Ejections (CME), Solar Flares (FLR), Solar Energetic Particles (SEP), and Geomagnetic Storms (GST). Relevant events can trigger alerts and educational scenarios explaining their potential impact on space missions.
  3. The Challenge System: Players encounter operational dilemmas involving radiation exposure, energy shortages, oxygen consumption, greenhouse production, water recycling, and lunar environmental conditions.
  4. Resource Allocation: Players manage limited resources and make strategic decisions to maintain the base. For example, they may redirect electrical power toward radiation protection during a solar storm, even if this reduces the energy available for food production.
  5. Interactive 3D Exploration: Players explore an immersive lunar environment featuring celestial objects such as Earth, Mars, the Moon, and the Sun, alongside interactive base modules and educational elements.
  6. Mission Evaluation: The game reflects the consequences of player decisions through updated resource conditions, mission feedback, and educational explanations that help players understand what happened and why.

Benefits & Educational Impact:

  • Making Space Science Accessible: The project transforms complex aerospace concepts into simple, interactive experiences suitable for children aged 8–12.
  • Learning Through Decision-Making: Players experience the consequences of their choices, developing critical thinking, planning, and problem-solving skills.
  • Real Scientific Data Integration: NASA's DONKI API connects gameplay to actual space weather information instead of relying exclusively on fictional events.
  • Understanding Astronaut Safety: Educational explanations introduce radiation exposure, solar storms, oxygen management, and other challenges associated with human space exploration.
  • Scientific Discovery Through Exploration: Interactive 3D environments encourage children to explore planets, lunar structures, and mission systems while learning about their functions.
  • Connecting Science with Everyday Decisions: Resource management demonstrates the importance of energy efficiency, water conservation, food production, and sustainable systems.
  • Learning Through Experimentation: Players can test different strategies, observe the results, and improve their decisions throughout the mission.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies Used:

  • Frontend Framework: React with TypeScript for building the interactive application, reusable components, and dynamic gameplay systems.
  • 3D Graphics & Rendering: Three.js and React Three Fiber for creating immersive 3D environments, celestial objects, and interactive lunar exploration elements.
  • Styling & UI: Tailwind CSS for responsive interfaces, custom layouts, and a playful claymorphic visual identity.
  • Animations: Motion for smooth transitions, interactive feedback, and animated interface elements.
  • Game State Management: Zustand and React Hooks (useState, useEffect) for managing game states, resources, mission progression, and interactive events.
  • Graphics & Icons: Custom SVG illustrations, CSS gradients, and visual effects for creating expressive interface elements and educational visuals.
  • Data Integration: Native JavaScript Fetch API for retrieving and processing information from NASA's DONKI open API.
  • Scientific Data Resources: NASA OSDR, RadLab, NASA Mars Trek, and Canadian Space Agency educational resources for scientific references and educational content.
  • Deployment Platform: Vercel or Netlify for browser-based deployment, allowing students and judges to access the experience without downloading additional software.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

  • Real Science Meets Interactive Gameplay: The project connects real space weather information with educational mission scenarios, helping children understand how scientific observations relate to astronaut safety and mission planning.
  • The Resource Trade-Off Principle: Every important decision requires prioritization. Players must balance the needs of different systems rather than relying on unlimited resources or risk-free solutions.
  • Accessibility for Young Explorers: Technical concepts such as Coronal Mass Ejections, radiation exposure, and oxygen consumption are translated into understandable explanations supported by visual feedback and interactive elements.
  • Exploration-Based Learning: The 3D lunar environment encourages curiosity and discovery, allowing children to interact with space objects and understand the purpose of different mission systems.
  • Educational Visual Design: The playful 3D aesthetic makes the experience approachable without losing its connection to real scientific concepts.
  • Mission-Based Progression: The 30-day mission structure gives players a clear objective and encourages them to develop better survival strategies as new challenges appear.
  • Scalable Educational Experience: The project creates a foundation for expanding AstroKids Academy with additional missions, scientific discoveries, space environments, and real-world data integrations.

NASA Data Utilized:

  • NASA Open APIs – DONKI Space Weather
  • Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI)
  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR)
  • RadLab – OSDR Radiation Dosimetry Database
  • NASA Mars Trek

Space Agency Partner & Other Data:

  • Canadian Space Agency (CSA) – Space Resources for STEM and Youth
  • Canadian Space Agency – Food Production in Space Educational Resources

Project Vision:

AstroKids Academy – Artemis-30 aims to inspire the next generation of explorers by transforming space science into an interactive learning adventure. By combining 3D exploration, strategic gameplay, and authentic scientific information, the project helps children understand the challenges of human space exploration while developing curiosity, creativity, and critical thinking. Train Today. Explore Tomorrow!
